# Feature: Turntable tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #7 (Turntable tile) from Movement Tiles before it is used in real levels. Effect: A framed tile that turns your on-foot movement 90 degrees, never a slide. Unique: the only tile that turns on-foot movement; slides and belts ignore it. Useful: bends a bounce launch around a corner without touching ice momentum. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** a framed tile that turns your on-foot movement 90 degrees, never a slide.

**So that** bends a bounce launch around a corner without touching ice momentum.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Turntable tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-7-turntable-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: a turntable stands before a junction, its arrow visible in the frame. A player who steps on it while thinking about the junction is nudged down the arrow's lane into a one-way stretch and has to loop back, which teaches that the framed arrow, rather than their next input, decides where it sends them on foot. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: The tile is drawn in a rotating frame with an arrow
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Stepping onto it on foot turns the arrow 90 degrees clockwise and nudges you one tile in the arrow direction, automatically on entry, nothing to press
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Sliding on ice or riding a conveyor passes straight over it: momentum and belt direction do not turn

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Turntable tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-7-turntable-tile-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/movement-tiles.yml mechanic #7.
